sections.heading: Reach your audience, right from your site.
body: Send email campaigns to your lists, put announcement bars and popups on any page, and A/B test what converts — all built into the same platform your site runs on.

body: Marketing usually means bolting on an email tool, a popup widget, and a testing script — each with its own dashboard and its own bill. Aglyn builds them into the platform, so your audience, your site, and your results live in one place.
sections.notes: Single full-bleed paragraph, 1280px wide, 80px gutters, 64px vertical padding. White background.

sections.heading: Everything to reach your audience.

items.title: Email campaigns
items.body: Design emails on the same canvas as your site, then send them to your lists — delivered through Resend.

items.title: Audience lists
items.body: Build and segment lists from your contacts. Every plan includes an audience band — and contacts past it are always captured and metered, never silently dropped.

items.title: Announcement bars
items.body: Put a scheduled bar at the top of any site for launches, sales, or notices (Starter and up).

items.title: Popups
items.body: Trigger popups by time, scroll, or exit intent, with frequency caps so they never nag (Starter and up).

items.title: A/B testing
items.body: Run experiments on screens and sections, and let the winning variant take over (Business and up).

items.title: Scheduled & measured
items.body: Schedule campaigns and overlays ahead of time, and see impressions and clicks on every one.

sections.notes: 3 columns × 2 rows, centred header — but UNLIKE Analytics the cards are NOT uniform height: card 1 is 229px, card 2 is 255px (its body runs to 4 lines), cards 3–6 are 203px. Row 2 starts at y=275 to clear the tallest card. Build with equal-height rows rather than reproducing the ragged Figma geometry. Section is white; same 410px card width and 44px icon square as Analytics. Card FRAME names are stale copies of the Analytics frame ('Card Traffic & pageviews', 'Card Cross-site rollups', 'Card Privacy-friendly' …) and contradict their own text — use the text nodes only.

sections.heading: Announcement bars and popups, without code.
body: Add a bar or popup to any site, choose when it shows — after a delay, on scroll, or on exit intent — and cap how often it appears. Schedule it for a launch, and take it down automatically.

items.title: Bars & popups

items.title: Smart triggers
items.body: Show on delay, scroll depth, or exit intent, with per-visitor frequency caps.

items.title: Scheduled windows
items.body: Set start and end times so overlays appear exactly when you want.

image.describe: Overlay editor mockup, 768×580. Breadcrumb 'Marketing / Overlays' with a 'New overlay' action. Top of the previewed site shows an announcement bar reading 'Aglyn is in early access — join the beta  →'. Below it a modal popup preview: 'Join the newsletter' / 'Product updates and early-access news.' / email field 'you@email.com' / 'Subscribe' button. Right rail is the overlay's settings: name 'Welcome popup' with a 'Live' status chip, then TYPE 'Popup', TRIGGER 'After 5 seconds', FREQUENCY 'Once per session', SCHEDULE 'Always on' — each a dropdown.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Build and segment lists from your contacts.
claimsToVerify.why: 'your contacts' implies a Contacts CRM, which Aglyn does not have. Banned-claim list: 'a Contacts CRM'. Reword to lists built from form submissions / subscribers if that is what actually exists.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Every plan includes an audience band — and contacts past it are always captured and metered, never silently dropped.
claimsToVerify.why: Two things to confirm: (a) 'contacts' again, per above; (b) a concrete billing/metering PROMISE about overage behaviour. Verify against the audience-band pricing implementation before publishing.
Names a third-party sub-processor in public marketing copy. Confirm this is intended and consistent with the privacy/sub-processor page, and that it stays true if the provider changes.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Run experiments on screens and sections, and let the winning variant take over (Business and up).
claimsToVerify.why: Automatic winner promotion ('let the winning variant take over') is a stronger claim than plain A/B testing. Confirm auto-promotion exists and that the gate is Business, not Pro.
'what converts' invokes a CONVERSIONS metric. Aglyn has no conversions metric. Banned-claim list: 'conversions/visitors metrics'.
Second conversion reference. Lower risk (it is positioning, not a named metric) but flagged for consistency with the conversions rule.

Uses 'visitor' as a unit of measurement. Confirm frequency capping is genuinely per-visitor (device/session identity) rather than per-session only — the mockup's own FREQUENCY field reads 'Once per session'.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Schedule campaigns and overlays ahead of time
claimsToVerify.where: Capabilities → card 'Scheduled & measured' (637:1280); also 'Put a scheduled bar…' (637:1258), 'Set start and end times…' (637:1307), 'send now or schedule it for later' (637:1323), mockup 'Schedule — Jul 28, 2026 · 9:00 AM'
claimsToVerify.why: Scheduled sending/display appears five times. Adjacent to the banned 'scheduled/cron triggers' claim. Confirm the scheduler actually fires (it is a different feature from workflow cron triggers, but it must exist).

claimsToVerify.phrase: and see impressions and clicks on every one.
claimsToVerify.where: Capabilities → card 'Scheduled & measured' (637:1280); echoed in step 03 'Track impressions, clicks, and opens'
claimsToVerify.why: Overlay impression/click and email OPEN tracking. Open tracking in particular needs confirming against the Resend integration and the 'cookieless, no tracker' privacy stance the Analytics page takes.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Track impressions, clicks, and opens — and A/B test to find what works.
claimsToVerify.why: Same open-tracking concern, plus a third indirect conversions reference ('what works').

claimsToVerify.phrase: Marketing works with the rest of Aglyn
claimsToVerify.why: Not a capability claim — a copy defect. Missing the trailing period that the sibling Analytics page has. Fix at sign-off.
Inconsistent with 'Eight products, one platform.' on the Product overview page and with the seven-card grid on this page. Same issue flagged on Analytics.
SELF-HOSTING CLAIM. Only 'Docker + your own Firebase project' is supportable. Appears on all three pages.
